audio_caption: The audio clip begins with a male speaker noting it's "Anzac Day today" and mentioning the Anzac Day weekend. He's camping and will show what he is doing. The speaker discusses looking for gold, noting, "There's a lot of flower gold here," and mentioning his preference for searching out-of-the-way crevices.

The clip begins with a male speaker discussing the effects of recent floods, noting "all the mud's been deposited." He then describes how he cleaned out the very start of something, explaining that it runs off into a sandbar and he'll follow it back that way, addressing another task later. The tone is casual and informative.

The audio features a male speaker describing his gold prospecting activities. He mentions using buckets and difficulty finding empty crevices, explaining how he stockpiles material to run through later, and how it helps keep water away from his work. The tone is casual and informative. There are also sounds of breathing in the background.

The audio clip features one male speaker with an Australian accent who starts by mentioning the number of days he has been working. He explains that he just cleaned out some crevices and describes his success, remarking he "did pretty good." He then notes a small crevice and mentions he got more gold from it than from the other areas. Ambient sounds of wind can be heard throughout the clip.

The clip starts with a male speaker explaining "the main reason." He points out a bedrock slide and a drainage point, noting how "everything" washes down there, including debris from past floods. He describes how "big floods" occur and everything runs into "that hole". Ambient wind sounds are present throughout.

The audio clip features a male speaker discussing finding gold in small spots, mentioning that even the small spots were "not too bad". He describes a "banker" running well, planning to get a wider one, and notes it's heavy. He also mentions his "Chinese pump" running well for nearly 18 months with only one issue: the oil cap blew off. He expects to return in a few days. The speaker's tone is casual and descriptive. In the background, there is the sound of running water.

The audio clip begins with a man speaking, his tone casual, remarking that it "will be interesting to see how far that crevice runs." He mentions digging and finding little gold, describing plans to clean the crevice, then shift focus to some rocks where someone else has already been prospecting. Throughout his monologue, ambient background sounds prevail, suggesting an outdoor environment.

The audio clip begins with someone speaking, suggesting they can just move next door. The speaker then remarks about a "big carp in this creek" and its size. The speaker notes the beautiful weather and comments that they will come back to clean it out after. This is followed by the sound of someone ringing a bicycle bell and some music, before the clip ends.

The clip features a single male speaker who is actively panning for gold, giving instructions and sharing tips in an enthusiastic and practical tone, including where to obtain equipment. The speaker also mentions finding a gold nugget the previous day and talks about processing the sediment. Splashing water sounds are constant and dominate the background, indicating the presence of a river or stream, with minor changes in intensity to highlight the panning activity. The speech then shifts to a more observational tone as the speaker describes the contents of his pan and the quality of the camera. He mentions seeing a significant amount of gold and struggles to zoom in.

The audio clip starts with a single male speaker, who appears to be observing materials collected from a shovel, expressing that "it's not all going to be as rich as right at the bottom of those crevices". He hopes the image shows up well and describes some bigger pieces and fine stuff. The speaker continues describing a crevice running all the way up and notes how the land looks, discussing the water's path during a flood. Background wind sounds persist throughout the speech, sometimes sounding rather strong.

The audio clip begins with male speech discussing how something "is going to find its way" and mentioning a "very last crevice." His tone is conversational and instructive. He continues, describing cleaning and washing, and the potential for "good goal." His tone remains optimistic and instructional. The clip concludes with what sounds like a windy ambient noise.

The audio clip begins with one male speaker discussing searching for gold, mentioning putting "tons and tons and tons of sand" through a process and exploring "big cracks and crevices". His tone suggests a methodical and possibly optimistic approach. He then states he'll continue and return when running a high banker. This is accompanied by continuous ambient sounds that suggests an outdoor, possibly natural environment. The clip then concludes.

The audio clip begins with a male speaker who says, "I've finished or cleaned out those crevices, unbelievably deep." He then says "Got some heave material there," indicating that he will continue along the crevice tomorrow. The speaker seems hopeful about the depth. Throughout this, background sounds of wind can be heard.

The audio clip begins with rustling sounds and speech, "have a look in the bank". A single male speaker strains while physically exerting himself. The rustling continues, accompanied by "Oh". The man continues speaking, saying, "There is definitely gold in there. I'm gonna hope there is lots, so I'll pull it down, come back and we'll see what we got".
